What document is typically created to launch a project?
A project charter formally authorizes the work and records its objectives, scope, stakeholders, and high-level responsibilities.
What roaming technology uses stored keys at the APs for roam back if a client STA returns after having roamed away?
PMK caching reuses previously established key material when a client returns to an AP, reducing authentication overhead and roam time.
What frequency and power did 802.11y provide?

802.11y enabled operation in the 3.65–3.7 GHz band with higher permitted EIRP in the applicable regulatory context. The frequency and power are regulatory characteristics, not a standard 2.4/5 GHz WLAN channel plan.

An amplifier has a 1 dB compression point of 32 dBm and a gain of 20 dB. Which is the highest average input power shown here that would be safe to operate a 24 Mbps 802.11g signal so that spectral regrowth is not a problem?
The 1 dB compression point is where an amplifier departs from linear gain. Keeping average input power at or below the stated safe level avoids driving the amplifier into compression.
What might limit the ability to locate 802.11 clients using a WLAN infrastructure without an 802.11 tag?
If a client is powered off, it emits no Wi-Fi frames for the infrastructure to hear; infrastructure-based location cannot determine its live position.

While performing a validation site survey, you realize that overlapping channels are being used on the 2.4 GHz bad due to the automatic channel assignment algorithm of the WLAN infrastructure. What should you do to prevent this?
Reconfigure the network to use static channel plans because automatic channel assignment algorithms are all broken
Purchase and deploy new APs from a different vendor
Reconfigure the automatic channel assignment settings to use only channels 1, 6, and 11
Leave it as it is; sometimes using all 11 channels in 2.4 GHz gives the optimum performance result
In the 2.4 GHz band, channels 1, 6, and 11 are the conventional non-overlapping 20/22 MHz channel plan in North America.
Which of the following items could be considered constraints when performing a network design?(Choose all that apply.)
Timeline, staffing, organizational politics, and budget can all constrain a WLAN project. They influence what can be designed and delivered.
After designing a WLAN infrastructure using predictive design software. What's the best way to validate the predictive design in the physical space before deployment, if time and budget allow for it?
Perform an AP-on-a-Stick survey using AP locations based upon the predictive design to confirm each AP's placement.
Deploy all of the APs as they're shown in the predictive design and perform a passive site survey.
Deploy all of the APs as they're shown in the predictive design and perform an active site survey.
Use a client device positioned where the APs will be installed and measure the signal from the client device.
An AP-on-a-Stick survey is a method of validating a predictive design by placing an AP at each
As a device starts to shift to lower PHY rates, what factors usually influence a device decision to shift to lower PHY rates?(Choose all that apply.)
PHY rate adaptation responds to link quality. Signal degradation, packet loss, interference, and retransmissions are all indicators that a lower rate may be more reliable.
Before performing a pre-deployment passive RF survey of a new deployment using survey mapping software, which of the following must be performed?
A predictive model needs a correctly scaled and calibrated floor plan so distances, wall locations, and attenuation are represented accurately.
What functions may be performed by a WIPS?(Choose all that apply.)
Client access to the distribution system
A WIPS can analyze wireless protocols, monitor performance, retain forensic data, and automatically mitigate detected wireless threats.
A table of VLANs in a _________ document should include what device performs ________ services.(Fill in the blanks)
The Low-Level Design (LLD) should identify VLANs and document which network device provides routing for each VLAN or subnet.
Prior to meeting with the customer for the first time, you should do which of the following?
Decide which vendor they will benefit most from.

Research the customer as much as possible. Try to understand what their business is, who their customers are, and any other information you can find regarding product lines and recent press announcements.
Find out what vendor their competitors use.
Plan an initial design to present to them.
Researching the customer's business, users, and operations before the first meeting helps uncover relevant requirements and ask informed discovery questions.
For an antenna 35 dBi of gain is needed. What antenna type should be used to achieve this gain?
A dish antenna concentrates RF energy into a narrow beam and can provide very high gain, making it suitable when approximately 35 dBi is required.
A museum wants to offer Wi-Fi to its visitors. One of their requirements is to have the APs blend into the design of the museum. What should you do to meet this requirement?
Use a plastic cover that could blend in with the environment
Lock the AP inside of a metal box
Place the APs in between walls and I-beams
Use an 802.11b AP, so it looks old enough to be in a museum
A purpose-designed nonmetallic cover can improve appearance while avoiding the severe RF attenuation caused by metal enclosures; manufacturer guidance and warranty terms still apply.
An MSA commonly addresses at least which two legal categories?
A nondisclosure agreement establishes a confidentiality obligation and limits how the customer's proprietary information may be shared.
How much more power can a 1 Mbps 802.11b signal have than a 54 Mbps 802.11g signal if it is sent through a saturated amplifier?
A 5 dB difference represents a factor of about 3.16 in power. Lower-rate legacy transmissions may be allowed higher transmit power under applicable device/regulatory limits.

An engineering firm just upgraded their WLAN from nine 802.11n APS to nine 802.11ac APs. After this upgrade, they did not see any improvement in throughput. What is the most likely cause of this result?
The APs are still using the 5 GHz lower band
APs are mounted on the wall
APs are transmitting at a low transmit power
A faster AP cannot deliver the newer PHY's benefits to legacy clients that lack the corresponding radio capabilities.
What are the two types of WLAN discovery/scanning?
Active scanning sends Probe Requests to discover APs; passive scanning listens for Beacon frames. These are the two basic WLAN discovery methods.

You are using site software design features. You have imported a floor plan, but the simulated RF coverage is nowhere close to the real RF coverage you see with a walkabout. Given that the simulation is significantly different, when step was likely missed when using the software?
Adding extra APs to simulate interference
A predictive model needs a correctly scaled and calibrated floor plan so distances, wall locations, and attenuation are represented accurately.
